Question: Does lying require more effort?
Old_Answer: More effort than the truth? Definitely, if you want them to be believed. You've got to remember what lies you told, to whom. You'll probably also need to come up with other lies too, to try and cover up the obvious discrepancies between known facts and the story you've just been telling, all without hesitation, repetition or deviation, and then you'll have to remember those lies too. Elaborate fiction at short notice will have to be your strongest skill. If you fail in any of these, your lies will be immediately obvious to everyone around you. No-one will trust you, for good reason, and you'll quickly acquire a reputation for being a liar and a fool. As even Presidents and Princes have discovered, you can't fool all of the people all of the time. On balance, the truth, told at the right time rather than when it's dragged out of you, may be painful and embarrassing, but it's a whole lot easier, and in the long term, will involve much less pain and shame.

Of course, this isn't to say that the truth doesn't sometimes require courage, especially when it involves difficult subjects or emotions. But overall, the mental energy expended in lying is usually greater, as it involves a level of deceit and anxiety that honesty simply does not. So, yes, lying does indeed require more effort.
